interest: This file provides valuable historical insight into Japan's extensive use of cultural diplomacy, soft power, and municipal boosterism during the 1930s—a period of increasing international isolation following its departure from the League of Nations. It illuminates the State Department's institutional policy distinguishing official government-sponsored events from municipal or commercial exhibitions, consistently declining official federal funding while facilitating commercial publicity through the Departments of Commerce, Agriculture, Labor, and Interior. Additionally, the records highlight Japan's diplomatic and commercial outreach across Latin America and the Philippines, and document the eventual postponement of the ambitious 1940 Tokyo International Exposition due to the escalation of the Second Sino-Japanese War.
overview: This file consists of Department of State docket sheets (Lists of Papers and jacket case sheets) for decimal file 894.607 ('Industrial Matters. Japan: Expositions. Exhibitions. Included All Expositions Of Whatever Character'), documenting U.S. diplomatic correspondence, interdepartmental circulars, and foreign intelligence concerning international expositions held or planned in Japan between 1931 and 1940. Major events cataloged across the sub-jackets include the 1931 Siamese Exposition and the 1933 Women's and Children's International Exhibition in Ueno Park, Tokyo; the 1935 Yokohama Municipal Exposition; the 1935 Osaka Commercial Museum exhibit; the 1937 Nagoya Pan Pacific Peace Exhibition; and the planned 1940 International Exposition of Japan in Tokyo commemorating the 2600th anniversary of the founding of the Japanese Empire. The docket entries reflect standard U.S. foreign policy declining official government participation and appropriations—frequently on the grounds that invitations were initiated by local promoters rather than the Japanese Imperial Government—while arranging for domestic executive departments to circulate publicity to private commercial exhibitors, as well as tracking Japanese promotional missions throughout Latin America until the 1940 Tokyo exposition was postponed.

subfiles.about: Master docket sheet and cross-reference list indexing communications and sub-jackets relating to exhibitions and expositions held in Japan between 1931 and 1940.
subfiles.summary: This master docket sheet (Form DS-46) cross-references seven key communications filed under decimal file 894.607 from 1931 to 1938. The items indexed include the 1931 Siamese exposition in Tokyo, the 1933 Women's & Children's International Exhibition, the 1935 Yokohama Municipal Exposition, the 1935 Osaka Commercial Museum exhibit, the 1937 Nagoya Pan Pacific Peace Exhibition, Japanese non-participation in the 1936 New York World Two-Way Fair, and the proposed 1940 Tokyo International Exposition. For each entry, the sheet directs researchers to specific sub-jackets or related decimal files.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Expositions — Japan (Decimal File 894.607)

subfiles.about: Four-page jacket case docket record tracking correspondence, interdepartmental circulars, and diplomatic reports regarding the 1937 Nagoya Pan Pacific Peace Exhibition.
subfiles.summary: This four-page jacket case list details 49 communications concerning the Nagoya Pan Pacific Peace Exhibition scheduled for March 15 to May 31, 1937. It records initial dispatches from Vice Consul Charles H. Stephan, promotional literature, and formal invitations transmitted by the Japanese Foreign Office and Embassy. Finding that the invitation was issued on behalf of exhibition promoters rather than the Japanese Government, the State Department declined official participation but coordinated with the Departments of Agriculture, Commerce, Interior, Labor, and Treasury to circulate publicity to prospective private exhibitors. The record also notes Prince Higashikuni's appointment as Governor, Latin American and Philippine missions, the opening of the exhibition, and 'America Day' festivities.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Nagoya Pan Pacific Peace Exhibition (Decimal File 894.607 Nagoya)

subfiles.about: Docket sheet recording a diplomatic dispatch regarding Dominican Republic participation in the 1935 Osaka Commercial Museum exhibition.
subfiles.summary: This jacket case sheet contains a single docket entry recording Despatch No. 2078 of December 13, 1934, from U.S. representative Brown in the Dominican Republic. It notes press reports stating that the Chamber of Commerce of Santo Domingo received an invitation to display Dominican products at the Osaka Commercial Museum from March 15 to April 4, 1935. The entry further records that an exhibition of Dominican goods was being prepared for shipment to Japan.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Osaka Commercial Museum (Decimal File 894.607 Osaka)

subfiles.about: Two-page docket record tracking diplomatic negotiations, policy discussions, and overseas promotional missions relating to the planned 1940 Tokyo International Exposition.
subfiles.summary: This two-page docket record catalogs 20 entries relating to the proposed International Exposition of Japan in Tokyo, planned for 1940 to commemorate the 2600th anniversary of Emperor Jimmu's accession. It documents invitations extended to the United States and Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, the State Department's decision that Grew decline serving as honorary counselor, and internal discussions concerning potential Philippine participation. The docket also records dispatches from American diplomatic posts in Cuba, British territories, Uruguay, and Brazil reporting on Japanese delegations soliciting participation, concluding in July 1938 with State Department acknowledgment of the exposition's indefinite postponement.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: International Exposition of Japan, Tokyo, 1940 (Decimal File 894.607 Tokyo)

subfiles.about: Two-page docket record documenting U.S. government responses and publicity efforts regarding the 1933 Women's and Children's International Exhibition in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: This two-page docket sheet lists 17 communications dated between August 1932 and March 1933 concerning the Women's and Children's International Exhibition held in Ueno Park, Tokyo. It traces Ambassador Joseph C. Grew's transmittal of the Japanese invitation, followed by declinations of official participation from the U.S. Departments of Labor and Interior and the American Red Cross due to a lack of congressional funding. It records assurances that foreign exhibits would receive duty-free entry, domestic press publicity generated by the Department of Commerce, and an account of U.S. Embassy officers attending 'American Day' at the exhibition.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Women's & Children's International Exhibition, Tokyo, 1933 (Decimal File 894.607 Women's)

subfiles.about: Preliminary typed docket list recording initial correspondence and departmental referrals regarding the 1935 Yokohama Municipal Exposition.
subfiles.summary: This sheet represents a preliminary draft typescript docket sheet for the Yokohama Municipal Exposition scheduled for March 24 to May 26, 1935. It catalogs correspondence between Consul Richard F. Boyce and the Mayor of Yokohama, notes transmitting regulations and pamphlets, and referrals to domestic executive departments. Responses from the Departments of Commerce and Interior indicate that while lack of appropriations precluded official government exhibits, notices would be published in 'Commerce Reports' and sent to regional trade bureaus.
subfiles.title: Draft List of Papers: Yokohama Municipal Exposition (Decimal File 894.607 Yokohama)

subfiles.about: Formal jacket case docket sheet recording correspondence and interdepartmental actions regarding the 1935 Yokohama Municipal Exposition.
subfiles.summary: This official Form DS-46 docket sheet formally records eleven communications dated between July and November 1934 concerning the Yokohama Municipal Exposition. Entries detail reports from Consul Richard F. Boyce transmitting maps, photographs, and regulations, followed by an invitation from the Japanese Embassy on October 13, 1934. The Department of State circulated the information to the Departments of Agriculture, Commerce, and the Interior, all of which noted a lack of federal funds for official exhibits but agreed to publicize the event to prospective American commercial exhibitors.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Yokohama Municipal Exposition (Decimal File 894.607 Yokohama)
